name: Frontal-orbital advancement (frontal bossing / brow)

lead: Frontal-orbital advancement, as the term appears in looksmaxxing, means pushing the brow and upper orbit forward for a more projected look. Forum discussion found concerns brow lifts and combined surgery trips.
The closest documented literature is facial feminization surgery, which mostly reduces the brow ridge, and brow-lift studies.

paras: Brow lifts change soft tissue position. Forehead contouring in feminization surgery grinds or reshapes bone over the frontal sinus. No source reviewed describes a cosmetic technique that advances the bone.

Wikipedia lists cranioplasty risks including improper bone healing, bone fragment movement and cyst formation, and thin sinus walls complicate grinding. Outcome data for forehead and orbit procedures are described as limited.

lead: In looksmaxxing usage, frontal-orbital advancement and frontal bossing refer to surgery or other changes meant to push the brow ridge and upper orbital area forward, producing a more prominent forehead and brow. The sources reviewed contain little direct material on this exact aim.

The nearest documented surgical literature is facial feminization surgery, which usually reduces rather than advances the brow ridge and forehead [1][2], and brow-lift procedures that change eyebrow position rather than bone projection [3][4]. No study of cosmetic frontal-orbital advancement in a non-craniofacial-condition population was found.
infobox: More forward brow and forehead projection
Brow lift, forehead contouring, orbital rim work

paras: Wikipedia's facial feminization surgery article describes the male brow ridge as typically more horizontal and solid, and procedures that grind it down, or reshape the bone above the frontal sinus when the sinus wall is thin [1]. It states that data on which forehead approach is better is limited, and that female orbits tend to be smaller and higher [1].

A review of facial feminization surgery describes it as a group of procedures changing a male face toward a female one, mainly for transgender women [2]. These procedures move in the opposite direction to the forward brow some looksmaxxers describe.

No studies found on cosmetic forward advancement of the brow and orbit for appearance. Related published work concerns brow lifts, including botulinum toxin brow elevation [3], endoscopic brow lift in 538 patients [4], and the direct brow lift [5].

Looksmax.org members post about brow lifts, often as part of combined surgery packages abroad with other procedures such as genioplasty, cheek implants and canthopexy [6]. These threads concern brow-lift surgery and recovery, not bone advancement.
